package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and Kubernetes credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, then exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, enabling theft of sensitive credentials.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py is executed automatically during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Access to sensitive files and exfiltration of credentials to an external server.

behavioral_signatures: Access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config during package installation.
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com from setup.py or installation scripts.
Presence of code in setup.py that reads sensitive files and sends their contents over the network.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor installation scripts (setup.py) for file access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, and for outbound network connections to app.threatest.com. Flag any package that attempts to read these files and send their contents to external servers during installation. Use static analysis to detect hardcoded references to sensitive file paths and suspicious network destinations in setup.py.
